findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback, unlike disconnectMutation below it which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations on settle. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes onChanged which may be undefined, so after a successful deletion the connectedCalendars query is not refetched, cacheUpdatedAt remains truthy, and the dropdown continues to show 'Cache Status' and 'Delete cached data' for cache that no longer exists until a manual reload.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache entries
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering on expiresAt, whereas getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now. After the one-month caching period expires, the UI will still report a 'Last updated' cache status and offer 'Delete cached data' for an entry that is never actually served, misleading users and support about whether cached availability is in effect.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hardcoded to en-US locale
findings.body: The timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) regardless of the user's configured locale obtained via useLocale. Non-English users will see US-style dates (e.g. 7/15/25) mixed into an otherwise localized UI; the formatter should use the active locale (and ideally be memoized rather than constructed on every render).

findings.title: Tunnel script is macOS-only and silently reports failure as success
findings.body: Line 68 uses BSD/macOS syntax `sed -i '' -E ...`, which fails under GNU sed on Linux ('' is treated as an input file), so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated there. Additionally, the failure paths at lines 46-58 call cleanup(), which unconditionally `exit 0`, so rate-limit and 'failed to extract URL' failures are reported to callers/CI as success. ENV_FILE is also hardcoded to ../.env, which only resolves correctly when invoked from a specific working directory.

findings.title: dev:cron depends on undeclared tsx fetched via npx
findings.body: The script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but tsx is not declared in this package's dependencies/devDependencies. In this Yarn-workspaces repo the command will attempt to download an unpinned tsx from the network at runtime, failing offline and introducing an unreviewed, unpinned executable into the dev workflow; tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency or the ts-node runner retained.

findings.title: deleteCache throws a generic Error instead of a tRPC error and has no tests
findings.body: When the credential does not belong to the user the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`, which tRPC surfaces as an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN client error, so the client can only show the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast and monitoring records a server fault for a routine authorization denial. The new mutation also ships without any test covering the ownership check or the deletion, so a future refactor could allow deleting another user's cache (prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany is keyed only by the input credentialId) without failing CI.
